summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 52% to ₹1,628 Cr with PAT of ₹143 Cr (8.8% margin); order book stands at ₹3,326 Cr with ₹2,200 Cr of bids pending results.
summary.overview: Rajesh Power reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,628 Cr (+52% YoY), EBITDA of ₹197 Cr (+59%, 12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹143 Cr (+48%, 8.8% margin). H2 FY26 revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹990 Cr, but H2 EBITDA margin (11.4%) and PAT margin (8.5%) were lower than full-year levels, which management attributed to billing mix. Order inflow for FY26 was ₹2,743 Cr and the unexecuted order book closed at ₹3,326 Cr, below the ~₹4,500 Cr previously flagged, which management blamed on delayed tender results. Receivables rose sharply to ~₹350 Cr, which management attributed to heavy March billing, and payables rose to about 58 days.

segments.name: Power distribution
segments.commentary: 71% of the ₹3,326 Cr order book (₹2,365 Cr). Management cites ~₹5,000 Cr addressable distribution opportunity in Gujarat, part of the robust infrastructure scheme. Competitors per bid: 4 to 6.

segments.name: Power transmission
segments.commentary: 29% of the order book (₹961 Cr). Pan-India push into Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Odisha, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand; Gujarat is 85-90% of the total order book. Competitors per bid: 3 to 4.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: Signed a 65 MW / 130 MWh standalone project for GUVNL on a build-own-operate, rental basis. Targeted IRR 10-12%; billing ~₹14-15 Cr per year; execution expected by September 2027, with Q1 FY27 mentioned as a possible earlier date.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of ~35-40% retained; management said 40% growth is planned for FY27 and roughly 40% CAGR over the next 3-4 years.
EBITDA margin guided at 11-12% and PAT margin at 8-9%, described as stabilised rather than rising.
FY26 order inflow target of ₹4,000-5,000 Cr targeted for the year ahead; closing order book target above ₹5,000 Cr for FY27.
Pending bids of ~₹2,200 Cr expected to conclude by end-May or first week of June 2026; combined bid book (~₹5,700-6,000 Cr) assumed at ~40% win rate.
Gujarat share of order book expected to move toward 80:20 (Gujarat:outside) in the near term from 85-90% today.
Working capital cycle of 30-40 days described as sustainable.
capex_capacity: BESS: capex estimated at ₹1.5-2.5 Cr per MW; project funded 70-80% by bank debt with the balance as equity (absolute equity amount not yet quantified).
BESS revenue: ₹1.89 lakh per MW, giving ~₹14-15 Cr annual billing on 65 MW.
First 400 kV GIS project for a private Gujarat client expected to commission in September-October 2026.
FY26 execution: 350+ feeders, 4,000+ ring main units, 1,200+ distribution transformers, 1,300+ km of cable laid; over 51,000 km of MVCC work under execution in Gujarat.
Projects are typically executed in 18-24 months; the company says upcoming mobilisation of a few projects is expected within the next 2 months.
demand_pricing: Addressable market claimed at ~₹14,000-15,000 Cr per year across Gujarat (GETCO ~₹4,000-4,500 Cr addressable from ~₹10,000 Cr annual capex; distribution ~₹5,000 Cr), Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Jharkhand, and railway traction substations.
Price escalation clauses cover most items; management says raw material (aluminium, copper) increases are passed through back-to-back with no margin impact.
Cable-jointer attrition cited at 2-3%. Labour camps are placed near sites and management reports no LPG/West Asia-related labour shortage.
Insurance surety bonds now used in ~8-10% of non-Gujarat orders and expected to rise as more states include the clause in tenders.
Current L1 position: about ₹210 Cr of pre-tax value (H1 FY26 figure was ₹808 Cr).

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables (~₹350 Cr) and inventory jump versus H1 and last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a short-term effect from very high March billing, with no BESS receivables and no client payment delays; standard terms of 45-60 days stay. About ₹150 Cr had been collected from the ~₹348 Cr receivables by the call date. Debtor days are ~78 and are expected to return to ~60 as billing evens out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall short of the ~₹4,500 Cr target for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no shortfall in execution; the ~₹2,200 Cr of bids submitted in Q4 are still awaiting tender results, expected by end-May or early June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 gross and EBITDA margins decline, and what is the normal range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to billing mix. It sees project-level EBITDA of 11-12% and PAT of 8-9% as the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall in H2 despite higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said corporate and project-management employee costs are not scaling with revenue. Its later figures showed employee cost rose from ₹43.9 Cr in FY25 to ₹59 Cr in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS economics (ownership, revenue, IRR, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company will own and develop the 65 MW / 130 MWh asset, with monthly rental billing to GUVNL from around September 2027. Targeted IRR is 10-12%. Management said margins should match transmission, and that it is not bidding for more BESS projects, preferring BESS EPC.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working-capital stress visible in creditors, MSME dues and short-term borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no working-capital stress. Payables stretched to ~30-day credit terms from vendors, and MSME outstanding of ₹87 Cr was paid within 45 days except where agreed terms exceeded that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 400 kV GIS project and 765 kV expansion a margin opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 400 kV GIS project with a private Gujarat client is due for commissioning around September-October 2026. It described the margin commitment as stabilised at 11-12%, not expanding.

risks_watch: Receivables of ~₹350 Cr and debtor days of ~78 (vs ~60 target) need to normalise in the next quarter.
Conversion of the ~₹2,200 Cr pending bids by end-May or early June 2026, plus the ₹4,000-5,000 Cr FY27 inflow target.
Gujarat concentration (85-90% of order book) and early-stage non-Gujarat transmission entries.
Rising surety bond requirements may affect working capital in new states.
Associate HKRP contribution fell in H2 due to customer site-readiness delays; recovery expected over the next year.
BESS project capex and equity requirement are not yet quantified; commissioning timeline is September 2027 (possibly Q1 FY27).
Payables stretched to ~58 days; sustainability of vendor credit terms is open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and execution, but defensive on working capital and order-book timing, attributing both to billing timing and pending tender results. Management avoided quantifying BESS equity, margins above the current range, and the FY26 H2 margin decline beyond billing mix.
key_quotes: So, we are confident on the execution, like we did this year.
There is no delay in any payment receivable from the client or customer.
So what we are committing is not a decrease in margin, but a stabilized margin.
No, we are sticking with our previously committed guidance. No revision.
